title: hardening: VS Code protected Accounts lines do not pass --protected-project, so the accounts CLI started there still looks claude and node up through the workspace (VS Code twin of task-55710898)
description:
Filed by architect-1dd28c7c on 2026-11-03 while planning task-55710898, which was split on the package seam to stay under QA's 400-net-LOC rule: that row changes the daemon's accounts CLI and the JetBrains Accounts lines; this row is the VS Code half plus the docs for the whole contract.

Objective
- task-55710898 gives the daemon's `accounts` CLI (packages/moe-daemon/src/accounts/cli.ts, claudeAuth.ts) a `--protected-project <path>` option. With it, every command that runs claude resolves claude only in absolute PATH entries whose real path is outside that project (MOE_CLAUDE_BIN, when set, must be an absolute file outside it). The claude child then runs with PATH rewritten to those entries, cwd = the home folder, and on Windows NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 and an absolute %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe for a .cmd shim. Otherwise it refuses with MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND or MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED and runs nothing.
- JetBrains (TerminalAgentLauncher.accountsCommandFor) passes the option on every protected route in task-55710898.
- VS Code does not pass it yet. AccountsTreeProvider.runCli (task-a6227f4e, landed f27a5f7d) pins the PowerShell and the node, but the CLI it starts still finds claude through the terminal's PATH and the workspace cwd, and on Windows a claude.cmd shim finds `node` in the workspace first.

Deliverable
- Under the protected profile (protectedAccountsTerminal returns a non-refused selection), runCli's words carry `--protected-project <workspace folder>` right after `--accounts-file <registry>`, on win32 and POSIX, in the typed line and the clipboard line alike. The folder must be the one protectedAccountsTerminal validated against. Prefer adding it to the AccountsTerminal selection (a `project` field set by protectedAccountsTerminal) over re-reading vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders in the provider, so the two cannot drift.
- A null selection (legacy) keeps lines and terminal options byte-identical.
- Docs for task-55710898's contract, written once both IDEs pass the option:
  - docs/MCP_SERVER.md, the accounts CLI bullet: the option, the lookup rule and both tokens;
  - docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: a cause-and-fix entry for both tokens;
  - docs/CONFIGURATION.md, the MOE_CLAUDE_BIN row: under the protected profile it must be an absolute file outside the project.

Not in scope
- The CLI itself and JetBrains (task-55710898).
- The POSIX default-profile terminal shell.
- Validating cli.script.
- .moe edits.

Verification (the planner adjusts the cp list to the plan's files): the two-leg snapshot gate of task-a6227f4e (Linux env -i node v24.21.0, then Windows cmd.exe; each runs npm ci, npm test and npm run compile in moe-vscode over a git archive of HEAD with the changed moe-vscode files copied in), then `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && npm run lint`.
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile every VS Code Accounts line (win32 and POSIX, terminal and clipboard) passes --protected-project followed by the workspace folder protectedAccountsTerminal validated, right after --accounts-file <registry>, proven by literal-line rows in moe-vscode/tests/windows-terminal-shell.test.cjs that fail when the option or its value is dropped.
A null (legacy) selection keeps Accounts lines and terminal options byte-identical: the existing W1-W3, W9, Q1, V2 and accounts-view rows pass unchanged.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md describe --protected-project, MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND and MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED as task-55710898 landed them, and say both IDEs pass the option under the protected profile.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3, part 1: docs/MCP_SERVER.md, section **Claude Account Rotation**, the **CLI.** bullet (about :3147-3152). Edit this bullet only, with the Edit tool. Match the section's terse nested-bullet style.

1. Commands sub-bullet: append `vm-token <id> [--remove]`. It mints or deletes the account's long-lived token for Moe VM jobs; it is in the CLI's USAGE (packages/moe-daemon/src/accounts/cli.ts:71) but missing here, and the new rule below names it.
2. Error tokens sub-bullet: append `MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED` and `MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND`.
3. After the `MOE_CLAUDE_BIN` sub-bullet, add one `--protected-project <path>` sub-bullet with short nested points. Each fact below is the landed behaviour; check it against the cited code as you write.

- Contract and callers:
  - It is the IDEs' protected-profile contract, so `help` (USAGE) does not list it (cli.ts:19-24).
  - Under the protected profile, both IDEs pass it right after `--accounts-file <registry>`.
  - JetBrains passes it on every Accounts route (TerminalAgentLauncher.accountsCommandFor): PowerShell and bash with the project folder, and WSL with the project's /mnt path.
  - VS Code passes it in its Accounts terminal line and the same clipboard line, with the workspace folder that protectedAccountsTerminal checked (AccountsTreeProvider.runCli).
- When it is resolved: lazily, once per run, and only by commands that run claude: login, logout, check, `vm-token <id>` (the mint) and `remove --sign-out`. list, add, help, a plain remove and `vm-token --remove` never resolve it.
- Which claude is used (claudeAuth.ts protectedClaudeCommand and localEntry):
  - Only absolute PATH entries are kept: on Windows drive-qualified, and still drive-qualified after the real-path resolve, so never UNC, device, rooted or drive-relative. An entry is kept only when its real path and every ancestor is not the project, compared by path (case-folded on Windows and macOS) or by stat identity.
  - claude is `MOE_CLAUDE_BIN` when that names a path, and the path must then be a local absolute file outside the project.
  - Otherwise it is that bare name (default `claude`) in the kept entries: PATHEXT on Windows, an executable file on POSIX.
- How the claude child runs:
  - PATH = the kept entries; cwd = the home folder (HOME, or USERPROFILE on Windows, else os.homedir()), which must be a local folder outside the project.
  - Windows adds NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1, and a .cmd or .bat claude runs under the absolute %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe.
  - A .js/.mjs/.cjs claude runs under the CLI's own node.
- Refusal: otherwise the command exits 1 before any folder, prompt, registry write or run, with one of these two messages.
  - `MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED: <reason>; nothing was run.` The reason names one of: the project is not a local folder; no absolute PATH entry is outside the project; the home folder is not a local folder outside the project; MOE_CLAUDE_BIN is not an absolute file outside the project; or cmd.exe under SystemRoot is not a local file outside the project.
  - `MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND: "<bin>" was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project <path>; nothing was run.`
- Without the option (the legacy profile), nothing changes.

Keep the addition to about 12 lines. Cross-link to the step-3 troubleshooting entry by its heading text, not by a computed anchor.

Error handling and accuracy: any fact you cannot confirm in the cited code is left out, never guessed. A test fact from task-55710898 (pw/pp/pc rows) is not quoted as a doc claim.
implementationPlan.note: MCP_SERVER.md CLI bullet: vm-token, both tokens, and a --protected-project sub-bullet with five points, checked against claudeAuth.ts and cli.ts.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3, part 2: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Edit only with the Edit tool.

(a) TROUBLESHOOTING. Add a new entry directly after `### Sign-in fails: MOE_ACCOUNT_NOT_SUBSCRIPTION, ... MOE_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND` (about :1072-1086) and before `### MOE_ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT ...`. Heading: `### Sign-in refused under the protected profile: \`MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED\`, \`MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND\``. Use that section's **Symptom:** / **Cause:** / **Fix:** form.

Symptom:
- Under the protected profile (`executionProfile` `verified-local`), in JetBrains or VS Code, the terminal tab that **Sign in**, **Check sign-ins** or **Sign out** (or **Sign out and remove**) opened ends with one of the two lines.
- Quote each line's fixed text exactly as claudeAuth.ts:147 and :171 print it, with <reason>, <bin> and <path> as placeholders.
- The account's state is unchanged, and nothing was written or run.

Cause:
- Both IDEs start the accounts CLI with `--protected-project <project>` under that profile. That keeps a project copy of claude, or of the node an npm claude.cmd shim starts, from running during sign-in.
- The CLI then takes claude only from an absolute PATH entry outside the project (on Windows, a drive-qualified one), or from a MOE_CLAUDE_BIN path outside it. It runs claude with PATH = those entries and cwd = the home folder.
- NOT_FOUND: no such entry holds claude. Examples: claude installed only inside the project, or reachable only through a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry, or through a share or a mapped drive.
- REFUSED: list the five reasons from claudeAuth.ts protectedClaudeCommand.
  - A network-share home folder is refused.
  - The cmd.exe reason applies only to a .cmd or .bat claude on Windows.

Fix:
- Install Claude Code outside the project and put its folder on the PATH the IDE terminal gets, or set MOE_CLAUDE_BIN to its absolute path outside the project.
- Keep the home folder on a local drive.
- Run the action again.
- Point to docs/MCP_SERVER.md **Claude Account Rotation** for the full rule.

(b) CONFIGURATION, the `MOE_CLAUDE_BIN` row (:23). Keep it ONE table line. Extend the description cell: under the protected profile, where both IDEs pass `--protected-project`, a path must be an absolute file outside the project, and a bare name is looked up only on absolute PATH entries outside it (`MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_REFUSED` / `MOE_PROTECTED_CLAUDE_NOT_FOUND`; see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, **Sign-in refused under the protected profile**). Leave the Default and Example cells as they are.

The merge-risk check for (b) is already done. WT-19 (task-b1ca54f2) is the only open row with unlanded CONFIGURATION.md hunks, and they sit at about :195-238, far from :23. If a newer row touches :22-24 by the time you land, say so in the completion summary (mem:gotcha-adjacent-line-edits-conflict-in-worktree-landing).

Error handling and accuracy: name only behaviour the code shows, and every heading must render as plain markdown (no HTML).
